title: Beyond the 956: Ian 'Molly' Meldrum, legendary Australian music broadcaster and 'Countdown' host, dies at 83
excerpt: Ian 'Molly' Meldrum, the Australian music journalist, broadcaster and record producer who hosted ABC's Countdown for 13 years and championed Australian music for six decades, died on November 23, 2026, in Melbourne. He was 83. His family confirmed he died peacefully after a long period of ill health.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Ian “Molly” Meldrum, the Australian music journalist, broadcaster and record producer who hosted ABC’s Countdown for 13 years and championed Australian music for six decades, has died at 83.

Meldrum died peacefully at 5:30 a.m. on Monday, November 23, 2026, at Epworth Hospital in Richmond, Melbourne, after a long period of ill health, his family said in a statement. That was Sunday, November 22, in the United States. His longtime friend and manager, Mark Klemens, also confirmed his death to The Guardian.

Born Ian Alexander Meldrum on January 29, 1943, in Orbost, Victoria, Meldrum became one of Australia’s most beloved entertainment figures. From 1974 to 1987 he presented Countdown, the ABC’s Sunday-evening music program, which he co-created — bringing the world’s biggest pop stars into Australian living rooms and giving homegrown acts a national stage. He also worked as a music critic, journalist and record producer, and later appeared in music segments on the variety show Hey Hey It’s Saturday.

Meldrum is survived by his longtime partner, Yan Wongngam; his brothers, Brian and Robert; and Morgan Scholes, whom he helped raise and regarded as his son. His family has asked for privacy as they grieve.

Sources: AAP; The Guardian; Billboard; Mumbrella.
